chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar and Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah, all from Safwan from Sa'id al-A'raj from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about two men who had intercourse with a slave girl during one period of purity (from menstruation). For whom would the child be? He said: For the one in whose possession she is, due to the words of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family): 'The child belongs to the bed (the one with whom she resides), and for the adulterer is the stone.'

key_terms.الْعَاهِرِ: The adulterer / One who commits fornication
key_terms.لِلْفِرَاشِ: To the bed (referring to the husband or owner)

ai.seo_question: How is paternity determined for a slave girl who has intercourse with multiple men during one purity period?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi articulates the foundational legal maxim 'Al-Waladu lil-firash' (the child belongs to the bed), attributing lineage to the man in whose possession the woman resides at the time of conception. In the context of slave girls, this ruling prioritizes the owner's right over other claimants, reflecting the Prophetic tradition cited by Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to resolve paternity disputes. This principle remains central to Shia jurisprudence for determining nasab (lineage) in cases of multiple partners.
